hook: 131 tablets unearthed in Turkey rewrite Hittite history today.

sections.voiceover: 131 tablets unearthed in Turkey rewrite Hittite history today.
sections.visual_cue: Close‑up of 131 ancient tablets stacked on a table.

sections.voiceover: In 2026 archaeologists at Kayalıpınar, Sivas uncovered 131 tablets from King Tudhaliya II. How do these tablets reshape Hittite daily life?
sections.visual_cue: Map of Turkey highlighting Kayalıpınar and Samuha, then zoom on tablets.

sections.voiceover: Yet UNESCO's register recognizes the Bogazköy archive as the only surviving Hittite record.
sections.visual_cue: Scroll of unread cuneiform symbols fading into a question mark.

sections.voiceover: The 131 Kayalıpınar tablets detail royal decrees and tax data. UNESCO added the Bogazköy archive to its Memory of the World register.
sections.visual_cue: Animated charts showing numbers, then UNESCO logo with archive plaque.

sections.voiceover: 131 tablets now rewrite what we know of Hittite life.
sections.visual_cue: Fade to a single tablet with the number 131 etched.
